title_en: China Yuanda Group Co., Ltd. v. China Light Industry Foreign Economic and Technical Cooperation Company — dispute over import and export agency contract
ruling_gist_en: Where a person, in the name of the entity with which he is associated, signs an economic contract with another party and causes economic loss to the other party which constitutes a crime, in addition to pursuing the criminal liability of the person in accordance with the law, the entity with which he is associated shall also bear corresponding civil liability for the economic loss caused to the other party in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
China Grand Enterprises Group Co., Ltd. v. China Light Industry Foreign Economic and Technical Cooperation Company — dispute over import agency contract

Ruling Summary

Where a person, acting in the name of his or her unit, enters into an economic contract with another person, causing economic losses to the other person that constitute a crime, in addition to investigating the criminal liability of the person in accordance with the law, the unit shall also bear corresponding civil liability for the economic losses caused to the other person in accordance with the law.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Ti Zi No. 128

Re-applicant (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance): China Grand Enterprises Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Floor 25, Block B, Grand Center, No. 5 Huizhong Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Hu Kaijun, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Jun, lawyer of Beijing Dingshi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shi Yingchun, staff member of China Grand Enterprises Group Co., Ltd.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): China Light Industry Foreign Economic and Technical Cooperation Company. Domicile: Zhongqing Building, No. 4 Qiyang Road, Wangjing, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wang Xiangyang, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Yu Xiangdong, lawyer of Beijing Huabo Jinlong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ma Jun, lawyer of Beijing Huabo Jinlong Law Firm.

The re-applicant, China Grand Enterprises Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Grand), applied for a retrial against the civil ruling (2011) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 4278 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case of dispute over import agency contract with the respondent, China Light Industry Foreign Economic and Technical Cooperation Company (hereinafter referred to as China Light Industry). This Court, on May 25, 2015, rendered the civil ruling (2014) Min Shen Zi No. 1316, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear this case, and the hearing has now been concluded.

On December 2010, China Grand filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, alleging: On July 21, 2008, China Grand and China Light Industry entered into an "Agency Agreement for Import Entrustment" (hereinafter referred to as the "Agency Agreement"), under which China Light Industry entrusted China Grand to import palm oil. During the performance of the agreement, China Light Industry successively paid RMB 13.76 million to China Grand through Shanghai Zhuzhule Condiment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhuzhule Company). China Grand, as agreed, opened an irrevocable letter of credit and actually paid USD 3,432,909.03, importing 2,749.825 tons of palm oil on behalf of China Light Industry. China Grand also paid import tariffs and VAT of RMB 5,479,338.03. In total, China Grand paid RMB 28,918,211 for the performance of the agreement, and after deducting the amount paid by China Light Industry, the outstanding payment amounted to RMB 22,193,204.22. Therefore, China Grand filed the lawsuit, requesting the court to order: 1. China Light Industry to pay the outstanding payment of RMB 22,193,204.22; 2. Agency fee of RMB 164,072.11; 3. Liquidated damages for late payment until the actual date of payment, totaling RMB 31,020,720.91; 4. China Light Industry to bear all litigation costs of this case.

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court found on hearing: China Grand is now suing China Light Industry based on the import agency contract. The entire process from the conclusion of the contract to the taking of the goods has been identified by the criminal case as a criminal act of Zhao Yuanzheng. Therefore, China Grand's claim for China Light Industry to assume contractual liability cannot be supported and should be dismissed. China Grand's contention that China Light Industry was at fault for the harmful consequences and should bear compensation liability may be pursued separately after its losses are clarified and under the correct legal relationship. The court then ruled to dismiss China Grand's lawsuit.

China Grand, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court, arguing: The first-instance ruling had unclear findings of fact. Zhao Yuanzheng, as the Assistant General Manager of the Trade Branch and Manager of the Second Department, was in charge of China Light Industry's oil import business, falling within the scope of "persons directly in charge and other directly responsible persons of the unit" under Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Crimes Involved in Economic Disputes" (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions"). The disputed "Agency Agreement" was signed between China Grand and China Light Industry, using China Light Industry's official seal, electronic key, and palm oil import quota to apply for an automatic import license from the Ministry of Commerce. Such conduct fell within the scope of "in the name of the unit" under Article 3 of the Provisions. Zhao Yuanzheng was convicted of contract fraud, and it can be found that his conduct met the requirement of "obtaining property and taking part or all of it for himself" under Article 3 of the Provisions. The first-instance ruling also erred in the application of law. The first-instance court, disregarding the fact that China Light Industry released the goods using its No. 6 contract seal, erroneously concluded that the ownership of the disputed goods vested in China Grand, and further concluded that China Light Industry should not be held civilly liable under Article 3 of the Provisions. This was an error in the application of law. China Grand requested the second-instance court to set aside the civil ruling (2011) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 00723 of the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, and to remand the case for retrial or to amend the judgment in accordance with the law.

The Beijing High People's Court found on hearing: According to the effective criminal judgment (2010) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 1278 of the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, it has been determined that China Grand was the victim in the case of Zhao Yuanzheng's contract fraud, and the judgment ordered the distribution of the frozen and seized money and property to China Grand on a pro rata basis, and also ordered the continued recovery of criminal proceeds for distribution to China Grand on a pro rata basis. Therefore, it can be found that China Grand's losses have been addressed in the criminal case. Now, China Grand is asserting civil rights against China Light Industry. Since the frozen and seized money and property and the continued recovery of criminal proceeds need to be distributed pro rata to China Grand, China Light Industry, and other non-party companies, and the distribution ratios and amounts have not yet been determined, the first-instance court's ruling to dismiss the lawsuit was not improper. As for China Grand's claim for compensation liability, the first-instance court also found that it could pursue this claim separately after the losses are clarified and under the correct legal relationship. In summary, China Grand's grounds of appeal could not stand and were not supported by the court. The first-instance ruling was correct and should be upheld. The court issued the civil ruling (2011) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 4278 on December 19, 2011: appeal dismissed, original ruling affirmed.

China Grand, dissatisfied with the above ruling, applied to this Court for a retrial, arguing: The original rulings had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law. According to Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Crimes Involved in Economic Disputes" (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions"), where a person directly in charge or other directly responsible person of a unit enters into an economic contract with another person in the name of the unit, and takes part or all of the property obtained for himself, constituting a crime, in addition to investigating the criminal liability of the person in accordance with the law, the unit shall bear civil liability for the consequences caused by the person's entering into and performing the economic contract in accordance with the law. China Grand requested the court to set aside the first and second instance rulings and to amend the judgment ordering China Light Industry to pay China Grand RMB 31,020,720.91 for the payment, agency fee, and liquidated damages for late payment, and to bear all litigation costs of this case.

China Light Industry submitted a written defense, arguing: The original rulings had clear findings of fact and correct application of law. China Grand's retrial application had no factual or legal basis. China Light Industry requested the court to dismiss China Grand's retrial petition.

This Court finds on hearing: From the perspective of the conclusion of the contract in this case, before signing the contract, China Grand conducted a credit investigation of China Light Industry's business premises. China Light Industry also provided China Grand with copies of its business license, organization code certificate, and import and export enterprise qualification certificate, all bearing its official seal. When applying for the import and export license for the palm oil involved in the case, China Grand used China Light Industry's electronic key to submit documents to the Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China and entered into a sales contract with the seller. Second, during the entire performance of the contract, China Light Industry affixed its No. 6 contract seal to three contracts: the Agency Agreement, the Sales Contract, and the Tripartite Agreement on Oil Offloading and Storage (hereinafter referred to as the Storage Agreement). China Light Industry also affixed a seal across the folds of the Sales Contract and its annexes. China Grand opened a letter of credit through the Bank of China for acceptance, and Dongguan South China Oil Industry Co., Ltd. issued a certificate to China Grand confirming that all the palm oil had entered its storage tanks. Therefore, the foreign trade agency contract has been fully performed. China Grand filed this lawsuit based on the Agency Agreement and Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Crimes Involved in Economic Disputes" (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions") (Fa Shi [1998] No. 7), which complies with legal requirements and should be heard as a civil case. Although Zhao Yuanzheng, an employee of China Light Industry, has been convicted of contract fraud by an effective criminal judgment, this individual's criminal act has no connection with the performance of the Agency Agreement in this case and cannot exempt China Light Industry from its civil liability in this case. The original rulings dismissing China Grand's lawsuit were improper and should be corrected.

In summary, the original first and second instance rulings had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law, and should be set aside. China Grand's grounds for retrial are valid. Pursuant to Article 198, Paragraph 2, and Article 200, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

1. The civil rulings (2011) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 00723 of the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court and (2011) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 4278 of the Beijing High People's Court are set aside.

2. The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court shall continue to hear this case.

Presiding Judge: Yin Yingshun

Acting Judge: Zhou Qimeng

Acting Judge: Song Bing

October 12, 2015

Clerk: Guo Kai

[Introduction of Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Yin Yingshun: born in 1971, Doctor of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2014.
